You are fixing findings from the final whole-branch review of Atlas Field Force's Phase 1 backend ("backend core"), on branch `feat/backend-core-phase1`, immediately before it merges to `main`. Every individual task already passed its own review — this is the last gate, covering things only visible at the whole-branch level.

Work from: /Users/taha/Documents/atlas-fieldforce (stay on branch `feat/backend-core-phase1`).

Read these first for context:
- /Users/taha/Documents/atlas-fieldforce/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-20-backend-core.md (the plan — Global Constraints section especially)
- /Users/taha/Documents/atlas-fieldforce/PLAN.md (Phase 1 checklist)
- /Users/taha/Documents/atlas-fieldforce/PROGRESS.md

Fix ALL of the following, each as its own commit (so the history stays reviewable), running the full test suite (`cd backend && uv run pytest -v`) after each fix to confirm no regressions, and `uv run ruff check .` to confirm lint stays clean:

## Fix 1 (Critical — blocks merge): tenant-isolation filter is never installed in the running app

`install_tenancy_filter()` (in `backend/app/core/tenancy.py`) is only ever called from test files — `backend/app/main.py`'s `create_app()` never calls it, so in a real running process the SQLAlchemy `do_orm_execute` global tenant filter is never registered. The plan's own Architecture section says tenancy is enforced by this filter "not by trusting each query author" — as shipped, that's false for the actual app.

- Add a call to `install_tenancy_filter()` in `create_app()` (`backend/app/main.py`) — call it once, e.g. right after creating the `FastAPI()` instance, before returning `app`. This is safe: register/login run with `current_tenant_id` unset (`None`), and the filter listener already early-returns when `current_tenant_id.get()` is `None` (verify this is still true by reading `tenancy.py`), so nothing changes for the existing register/login/refresh/me flows.
- Write a regression test at the ROUTER level (not just the existing unit-level `tests/core/test_tenancy.py`, which installs the filter manually and would pass even without this fix) proving the filter is live through the actual app: register a user in tenant A, register a different user in tenant B, then — using whatever the app currently exposes (there's no cross-tenant list endpoint yet in Phase 1, so you'll need to prove this a different way, e.g. directly querying via the app's `get_db`-overridden test session with `current_tenant_id` set to tenant A after a request completes and confirming a manual `select(User)` only returns tenant A's row — OR, simpler and more direct: add a tiny assertion inside an existing test that after the TestClient's `app` fixture is constructed, `install_tenancy_filter`'s idempotency flag is set / the listener is registered on the `Session` class). Use your judgment on the cleanest way to prove "the filter is registered and live in the actual `create_app()` output," not just "the filter mechanism works in isolation" (Task 2 already proved the mechanism works — this test's job is to prove it's actually wired in). If you genuinely cannot find a clean way to test "is a SQLAlchemy event listener registered on this Session class" from outside `tenancy.py`, at minimum add a test that calls `create_app()` and then asserts `tenancy._installed is True` (import the module, check the flag) — imperfect but real, and better than nothing. Explain your choice in your report.

## Fix 2 (Important): `created_at` is naive `DateTime`, fed timezone-aware Python values

`backend/app/auth/models.py`'s `User.created_at` default is `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (aware), but the Alembic migration (in `backend/alembic/versions/`) creates the column as `sa.DateTime()` (naive) — this works silently on SQLite (all current tests pass) but will misbehave on real Postgres+asyncpg (aware→naive column mismatch). Fix:
- Change `sa.DateTime()` to `sa.DateTime(timezone=True)` in the existing migration file (edit it directly — this hasn't shipped to any real database yet, so editing in place is correct; do NOT create a new migration for an unreleased column).
- No model-code change needed if `Mapped[datetime]` already maps correctly, but check `backend/app/auth/models.py` — if the column type is implicit (inferred from the Python type), you may need an explicit `mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), ...)` to keep the model and migration in sync. Verify migration and model agree.
- Run the existing migration-verification step: `cd backend && DATABASE_URL="sqlite+aiosqlite:///./alembic_check.db" uv run alembic upgrade head && rm -f alembic_check.db` to confirm the edited migration still applies cleanly.

## Fix 3 (Important): JWT secret has a length validator but no "don't use the default in production" guard

`backend/app/config.py`'s `Settings.jwt_secret` default is a real, long (66-char) string that's public in source — fine for local dev, dangerous if a production deploy forgets to set `JWT_SECRET` (anyone could forge tokens for any tenant/role, since they'd know the exact default from the source). Add a check: if `environment != "development"` and `jwt_secret` equals the literal class default value, raise a `ValueError` at `Settings` construction time (same pydantic v2 validator pattern already used for the length check — extend it or add a second `field_validator`, whichever fits the existing code better). Write a test proving: `Settings(environment="production")` with no `jwt_secret` override raises; `Settings(environment="production", jwt_secret="some-other-32-plus-byte-value")` does not raise; `Settings()` (default `environment="development"`) does not raise even with the default secret.

## Fix 4 (Minor, security hardening): timing-based user enumeration in `authenticate()`

`backend/app/auth/service.py`'s `authenticate()` returns `None` immediately for an unknown email, before calling `verify_password` — so "unknown email" responds fast while "known email, wrong password" pays the argon2 hashing cost, letting an attacker enumerate registered emails by timing. Fix: when no user is found, still call `verify_password` against a dummy/precomputed hash (so the timing cost is paid either way) before returning `None`. Write a test that at minimum confirms behavior is unchanged for the existing cases (unknown email → None, wrong password → None, correct → user) — a true timing-attack test is out of scope for unit tests, just prove the dummy-hash call path doesn't break anything.

## Fix 5 (Minor): DRY — duplicated tenant+email query

`select(User).where(User.tenant_id == tenant_id, User.email == email)` appears verbatim in both `register()` and `authenticate()` in `backend/app/auth/service.py`. Extract a small private helper (e.g. `async def _get_by_tenant_email(db, tenant_id, email) -> User | None`) and use it in both places. No behavior change — existing tests must still pass unchanged.

## Fix 6 (Minor): uncaught `uuid.UUID(payload["sub"])` could 500 instead of 401

In `backend/app/auth/deps.py` (`get_current_user`) and `backend/app/auth/service.py` (`get_user_from_refresh_token`), `uuid.UUID(payload["sub"])` isn't wrapped in error handling — a token with a non-UUID `sub` claim would raise an uncaught `ValueError` (500) instead of the intended 401/domain-exception. Wrap it (catch `ValueError`, treat as invalid token → same 401/`InvalidRefreshTokenError` path already used for other invalid-token cases). Add a test for at least one of the two call sites proving a malformed `sub` claim now produces the expected error instead of a 500 — you'll likely need to hand-craft a token with a bad `sub` (e.g. `jwt.encode({"sub": "not-a-uuid", "type": "access", ...}, settings.jwt_secret, algorithm="HS256")` using the real secret, or find another way to get a validly-signed-but-malformed-payload token).

## Fix 7: update docs to reflect what's actually built

- `PLAN.md`: tick boxes 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4 (all of Phase 1 is now done).
- `PROGRESS.md`: append a new line (don't replace the existing one) summarizing Phase 1 completion — mention what was built (FastAPI skeleton, tenant-scoped models with the filter now actually wired into the app, JWT auth for rep/manager roles, event bus, job runner, docker-compose, CI) and that final review caught and fixed the tenancy-filter-not-installed gap plus the other hardening items above. Note next step: plan Phase 2 (zones & geofencing) fresh against this actual code.

## When you're done

Run the full suite one final time (`cd backend && uv run pytest -v`) and `uv run ruff check .`, confirm both clean, and report:
- Each fix's commit (short SHA + subject)
- Final test count (should be higher than 43, given new tests added)
- Ruff status
- Any concerns, especially about Fix 1's regression-test approach (be honest if you think it's weak — this is the load-bearing fix)

Write your full report to /Users/taha/Documents/atlas-fieldforce/.superpowers/sdd/final-review-fix-report.md with full detail per fix (what changed, test evidence). Then reply with ONLY a summary under 20 lines: status, list of commit SHAs+subjects, final test count, ruff status, concerns, report file path.

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications with a `ponytail:` comment (`// ponytail: this exists`), simple reads as intent, not ignorance. Shortcut with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic)? The comment names the ceiling and the upgrade path: `# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`.

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.
"}}

1	# Backend Core Implementation Plan
2	
3	> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
4	
5	**Goal:** Stand up the FastAPI backend skeleton for Atlas Field Force with working multi-tenancy, auth (rep/manager JWT login), an in-process event bus, and an in-process background job runner — the foundation every later subsystem (zones, pings, visits, tasks, goals, alerts) builds on.
6	
7	**Architecture:** Single FastAPI app (`backend/app/`), SQLAlchemy 2.0 async ORM, Postgres in production / SQLite (aiosqlite) in tests. Tenancy is enforced by a SQLAlchemy `do_orm_execute` global filter keyed off a per-request ContextVar, not by trusting each query author. Service layer owns logic; routers stay thin; models carry no business logic.
8	
9	**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, `uv`, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async), asyncpg (runtime) / aiosqlite (tests), Alembic, Pydantic v2 + pydantic-settings, argon2-cffi, PyJWT, uvicorn, pytest + pytest-asyncio + httpx, ruff.
10	
11	## Global Constraints
12	
13	- Python 3.12, dependency manager `uv` (`uv.lock` committed) — per `docs/design.md` Stack section.
14	- SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed async ORM; Postgres-first, SQLite-compatible for tests — per `docs/design.md` Stack section.
15	- `tenant_id` on every table from day one — per `docs/design.md` Core data model note.
16	- Service layer owns business rules; routers thin; models logic-free — per `docs/design.md` Stack section ("Internal module anatomy").
17	- No PostGIS, no WebSocket/SSE infra — per `docs/design.md` (Geofencing, Real-time model sections); not relevant to this plan directly but keep all choices in this plan consistent with that (plain SQL types only).
18	- Two roles: `rep`, `manager` — per `docs/design.md` Auth section.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## File Structure
23	
24	```
25	backend/
26	  pyproject.toml
27	  alembic.ini
28	  .env.example
29	  alembic/
30	    env.py
31	    script.py.mako
32	    versions/            (empty until Task 5's migration)
33	  app/

37	    db.py                 # async engine, session maker, Base, get_db dependency
38	    core/
39	      __init__.py

41	      security.py          # argon2 hash/verify, JWT encode/decode

48	      service.py            # register(), authenticate(), refresh(), get_user_by_id()
49	      router.py              # POST /register, /login, /refresh, GET /me
50	      deps.py                 # get_current_user, get_current_tenant (sets ContextVar)
51	  tests/

53	    core/

65	```
66	
67	**Interfaces summary (for cross-task consistency):**
68	- `app.db.Base` — SQLAlchemy `DeclarativeBase` subclass, all models inherit from it.
69	- `app.db.get_db() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]` — FastAPI dependency.
70	- `app.core.tenancy.TenantScopedMixin` — mixin providing `tenant_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID]`.
71	- `app.core.tenancy.current_tenant_id: ContextVar[uuid.UUID | None]`.
72	- `app.core.security.hash_password(password: str) -> str`, `verify_password(password: str, hashed: str) -> bool`.
73	- `app.core.security.create_access_token(subject: str, role: str, tenant_id: str) -> str`, `create_refresh_token(subject: str) -> str`, `decode_token(token: str) -> dict`.
74	- `app.core.events.EventBus.subscribe(event_type: str, handler: Callable[[dict], None]) -> None`, `.publish(event_type: str, payload: dict) -> None`.
75	- `app.core.jobs.JobRunner.register(name: str, func: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]) -> None`, `.run(name: str) -> None` (awaits the job once, on demand).
76	- `app.auth.models.User` — columns: `id: Mapped[uuid.UUID]` (PK), `tenant_id` (via mixin), `email: Mapped[str]`, `hashed_password: Mapped[str]`, `role: Mapped[str]` (`"rep"` or `"manager"`), `created_at: Mapped[datetime]`.
77	- `app.auth.service.register(db, tenant_id, email, password, role) -> User`, `authenticate(db, tenant_id, email, password) -> User | None`.

448	                lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == tenant_id,
449	                include_aliases=True,
450	            )
451	        )

589	    payload = {
590	        "sub": subject,
591	        "role": role,
592	        "tenant_id": tenant_id,
593	        "type": "access",
594	        "exp": datetime.now(timezone.utc) + delta,
595	    }
596	    return jwt.encode(payload, settings.jwt_secret, algorithm="HS256")

598

600	    settings = get_settings()
601	    delta = expires_delta or timedelta(days=settings.jwt_refresh_ttl_days)
602	    payload = {
603	        "sub": subject,

# Backend Core Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Stand up the FastAPI backend skeleton for Atlas Field Force with working multi-tenancy, auth (rep/manager JWT login), an in-process event bus, and an in-process background job runner — the foundation every later subsystem (zones, pings, visits, tasks, goals, alerts) builds on.

**Architecture:** Single FastAPI app (`backend/app/`), SQLAlchemy 2.0 async ORM, Postgres in production / SQLite (aiosqlite) in tests. Tenancy is enforced by a SQLAlchemy `do_orm_execute` global filter keyed off a per-request ContextVar, not by trusting each query author. Service layer owns logic; routers stay thin; models carry no business logic.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, `uv`, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async), asyncpg (runtime) / aiosqlite (tests), Alembic, Pydantic v2 + pydantic-settings, argon2-cffi, PyJWT, uvicorn, pytest + pytest-asyncio + httpx, ruff.

## Global Constraints

- Python 3.12, dependency manager `uv` (`uv.lock` committed) — per `docs/design.md` Stack section.
- SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed async ORM; Postgres-first, SQLite-compatible for tests — per `docs/design.md` Stack section.
- `tenant_id` on every table from day one — per `docs/design.md` Core data model note.
- Service layer owns business rules; routers thin; models logic-free — per `docs/design.md` Stack section ("Internal module anatomy").
- No PostGIS, no WebSocket/SSE infra — per `docs/design.md` (Geofencing, Real-time model sections); not relevant to this plan directly but keep all choices in this plan consistent with that (plain SQL types only).
- Two roles: `rep`, `manager` — per `docs/design.md` Auth section.

---

## File Structure

```

    auth/

**Interfaces summary (for cross-task consistency):**
- `app.db.Base` — SQLAlchemy `DeclarativeBase` subclass, all models inherit from it.
- `app.db.get_db() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]` — FastAPI dependency.

- `app.core.tenancy.current_tenant_id: ContextVar[uuid.UUID | None]`.
- `app.core.security.hash_password(password: str) -> str`, `verify_password(password: str, hashed: str) -> bool`.
- `app.core.security.create_access_token(subject: str, role: str, tenant_id: str) -> str`, `create_refresh_token(subject: str) -> str`, `decode_token(token: str) -> dict`.
- `app.core.events.EventBus.subscribe(event_type: str, handler: Callable[[dict], None]) -> None`, `.publish(event_type: str, payload: dict) -> None`.
- `app.core.jobs.JobRunner.register(name: str, func: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]) -> None`, `.run(name: str) -> None` (awaits the job once, on demand).

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker, create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase

from app.config import get_settings


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


settings = get_settings()
engine = create_async_engine(settings.database_url, echo=False)
async_session_maker = async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)


async def get_db() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    async with async_session_maker() as session:
        yield session

# backend/app/core/tenancy.py
import contextvars
import uuid

from sqlalchemy import event
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, Session, mapped_column, with_loader_criteria

current_tenant_id: contextvars.ContextVar[uuid.UUID | None] = contextvars.ContextVar(
    "current_tenant_id", default=None
)


class TenantScopedMixin:
    tenant_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(nullable=False, index=True)


_installed = False


def install_tenancy_filter() -> None:
    """Registers a global SELECT filter scoping every TenantScopedMixin query
    to current_tenant_id. Idempotent — safe to call more than once (e.g. once
    per test)."""
    global _installed
    if _installed:
        return

    @event.listens_for(Session, "do_orm_execute")
    def _apply_tenant_filter(execute_state):
        if not execute_state.is_select:
            return
        tenant_id = current_tenant_id.get()
        if tenant_id is None:
            return
        execute_state.statement = execute_state.statement.options(
            with_loader_criteria(
                TenantScopedMixin,
                lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == tenant_id,
                include_aliases=True,
            )
        )

    _installed = True
```

# backend/app/core/security.py
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import jwt
from argon2 import PasswordHasher
from argon2.exceptions import VerifyMismatchError

from app.config import get_settings

_hasher = PasswordHasher()


def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
    return _hasher.hash(password)


def verify_password(password: str, hashed: str) -> bool:
    try:
        return _hasher.verify(hashed, password)
    except VerifyMismatchError:
        return False


def create_access_token(
    subject: str, role: str, tenant_id: str, expires_delta: timedelta | None = None
) -> str:
    settings = get_settings()
    delta = expires_delta or timedelta(minutes=settings.jwt_access_ttl_minutes)
    payload = {
        "sub": subject,
        "role": role,
        "tenant_id": tenant_id,
        "type": "access",
        "exp": datetime.now(timezone.utc) + delta,
    }
    return jwt.encode(payload, settings.jwt_secret, algorithm="HS256")


def create_refresh_token(subject: str, expires_delta: timedelta | None = None) -> str:
    settings = get_settings()
    delta = expires_delta or timedelta(days=settings.jwt_refresh_ttl_days)
    payload = {
        "sub": subject,
        "type": "refresh",
        "exp": datetime.now(timezone.utc) + delta,
    }
    return jwt.encode(payload, settings.jwt_secret, algorithm="HS256")


def decode_token(token: str) -> dict:
    settings = get_settings()
    return jwt.decode(token, settings.jwt_secret, algorithms=["HS256"])
```

# backend/app/auth/service.py
import uuid

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.auth.models import User
from app.core.security import hash_password, verify_password


class EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(Exception):
    pass


async def register(
    db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str, password: str, role: str
) -> User:
    existing = await db.execute(
        select(User).where(User.tenant_id == tenant_id, User.email == email)
    )
    if existing.scalar_one_or_none() is not None:
        raise EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(email)

    user = User(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        email=email,
        hashed_password=hash_password(password),
        role=role,
    )
    db.add(user)
    await db.commit()
    await db.refresh(user)
    return user


async def authenticate(
    db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str, password: str
) -> User | None:
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.tenant_id == tenant_id, User.email == email))
    user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if user is None:
        return None
    if not verify_password(password, user.hashed_password):
        return None
    return user


async def get_user_by_id(db: AsyncSession, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> User | None:
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()

import uuid

import jwt
from fastapi import Depends, Header, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="/api/v1/auth/login", auto_error=False)


async def get_tenant_id(x_tenant_id: str = Header(...)) -> uuid.UUID:
    try:
        return uuid.UUID(x_tenant_id)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST, detail="invalid tenant id") from exc


async def get_current_user(
    token: str | None = Depends(oauth2_scheme),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> User:
    credentials_error = HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
        detail="could not validate credentials",
        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
    )
    if token is None:
        raise credentials_error

    try:
        payload = decode_token(token)
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
        raise credentials_error from exc

    if payload.get("type") != "access":
        raise credentials_error

    user = await get_user_by_id(db, uuid.UUID(payload["sub"]))
    if user is None:
        raise credentials_error

    current_tenant_id.set(user.tenant_id)
    return user

# backend/app/auth/router.py
import uuid

import jwt
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status
from pydantic import BaseModel
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.auth.deps import get_current_user, get_tenant_id
from app.auth.models import User
from app.auth.schemas import LoginRequest, RegisterRequest, TokenPair, UserOut
from app.auth.service import EmailAlreadyRegisteredError, authenticate, get_user_by_id, register
from app.core.security import create_access_token, create_refresh_token, decode_token
from app.db import get_db

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/auth", tags=["auth"])


def _token_pair_for(user: User) -> TokenPair:
    return TokenPair(
        access_token=create_access_token(
            subject=str(user.id), role=user.role, tenant_id=str(user.tenant_id)
        ),
        refresh_token=create_refresh_token(subject=str(user.id)),
    )


@router.post("/register", response_model=TokenPair, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def register_endpoint(
    body: RegisterRequest,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID = Depends(get_tenant_id),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> TokenPair:
    try:
        user = await register(
            db, tenant_id=tenant_id, email=body.email, password=body.password, role=body.role
        )
    except EmailAlreadyRegisteredError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT, detail="email already registered") from exc
    return _token_pair_for(user)


@router.post("/login", response_model=TokenPair)
async def login_endpoint(
    body: LoginRequest,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID = Depends(get_tenant_id),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> TokenPair:
    user = await authenticate(db, tenant_id=tenant_id, email=body.email, password=body.password)
    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="invalid credentials")
    return _token_pair_for(user)


class RefreshRequest(BaseModel):
    refresh_token: str


@router.post("/refresh", response_model=TokenPair)
async def refresh_endpoint(body: RefreshRequest, db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)) -> TokenPair:
    try:
        payload = decode_token(body.refresh_token)
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="invalid refresh token") from exc

    if payload.get("type") != "refresh":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="invalid refresh token")

    user = await get_user_by_id(db, uuid.UUID(payload["sub"]))
    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="invalid refresh token")

    return _token_pair_for(user)


@router.get("/me", response_model=UserOut)
async def me_endpoint(current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)) -> User:
    return current_user

# backend/app/core/events.py
from collections import defaultdict
from collections.abc import Callable


class EventBus:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._handlers: dict[str, list[Callable[[dict], None]]] = defaultdict(list)

    def subscribe(self, event_type: str, handler: Callable[[dict], None]) -> None:
        self._handlers[event_type].append(handler)

    def publish(self, event_type: str, payload: dict) -> None:
        for handler in self._handlers.get(event_type, []):
            handler(payload)


event_bus = EventBus()

# backend/app/core/jobs.py
import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable


class JobRunner:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._jobs: dict[str, Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]] = {}
        self._periodic_tasks: list[asyncio.Task] = []

    def register(self, name: str, func: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]) -> None:
        self._jobs[name] = func

    async def run(self, name: str) -> None:
        await self._jobs[name]()

    def start_periodic(self, name: str, interval_seconds: float) -> None:
        async def _loop():
            while True:
                await asyncio.sleep(interval_seconds)
                await self.run(name)

        self._periodic_tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(_loop()))

    async def stop_all(self) -> None:
        for task in self._periodic_tasks:
            task.cancel()
        for task in self._periodic_tasks:
            try:
                await task
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                pass
        self._periodic_tasks.clear()


job_runner = JobRunner()
```

import uuid

import jwt
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.auth.models import User
from app.core.security import decode_token, hash_password, verify_password


class EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(Exception):
    pass


class InvalidRefreshTokenError(Exception):
    pass


async def register(
    db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str, password: str, role: str
) -> User:
    existing = await db.execute(
        select(User).where(User.tenant_id == tenant_id, User.email == email)
    )
    if existing.scalar_one_or_none() is not None:
        raise EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(email)

    user = User(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        email=email,
        hashed_password=hash_password(password),
        role=role,
    )
    db.add(user)
    try:
        await db.commit()
    except IntegrityError:
        await db.rollback()
        raise EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(email)
    await db.refresh(user)
    return user


async def authenticate(
    db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str, password: str
) -> User | None:
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.tenant_id == tenant_id, User.email == email))
    user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if user is None:
        return None
    if not verify_password(password, user.hashed_password):
        return None
    return user


async def get_user_by_id(db: AsyncSession, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> User | None:
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()


async def get_user_from_refresh_token(db: AsyncSession, refresh_token: str) -> User:
    """Validates a refresh token and returns the user it belongs to.

    Raises InvalidRefreshTokenError if the token is malformed, expired, not a
    refresh token (e.g. an access token was passed instead), or the user no
    longer exists.
    """
    try:
        payload = decode_token(refresh_token)
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError() from exc

    if payload.get("type") != "refresh":
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError()

    user = await get_user_by_id(db, uuid.UUID(payload["sub"]))
    if user is None:
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError()

    return user

import uuid
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

import jwt
from fastapi import Depends, Header, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.auth.models import User
from app.auth.service import get_user_by_id
from app.core.security import decode_token
from app.core.tenancy import current_tenant_id
from app.db import get_db

oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="/api/v1/auth/login", auto_error=False)


async def get_tenant_id(x_tenant_id: str = Header(...)) -> uuid.UUID:
    try:
        return uuid.UUID(x_tenant_id)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST, detail="invalid tenant id") from exc


async def get_current_user(
    token: str | None = Depends(oauth2_scheme),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> AsyncIterator[User]:
    credentials_error = HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
        detail="could not validate credentials",
        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
    )
    if token is None:
        raise credentials_error

    try:
        payload = decode_token(token)
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
        raise credentials_error from exc

    if payload.get("type") != "access":
        raise credentials_error

    user = await get_user_by_id(db, uuid.UUID(payload["sub"]))
    if user is None:
        raise credentials_error

    # Scope current_tenant_id to this request only. FastAPI runs a yield
    # dependency's post-yield code as teardown after the route handler
    # returns, so the reset always fires - unlike a plain `return`, which
    # would leave the ContextVar set for whatever runs next in this context.
    reset_token = current_tenant_id.set(user.tenant_id)
    try:
        yield user
    finally:
        current_tenant_id.reset(reset_token)

import uuid

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import String
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.core.tenancy import TenantScopedMixin, current_tenant_id, install_tenancy_filter
from app.db import Base

pytestmark = pytest.mark.asyncio


class Widget(Base, TenantScopedMixin):
    __tablename__ = "test_widgets"

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)


async def test_query_only_returns_rows_for_current_tenant(db_session):
    install_tenancy_filter()

    tenant_a = uuid.uuid4()
    tenant_b = uuid.uuid4()

    db_session.add_all(
        [
            Widget(id=uuid.uuid4(), tenant_id=tenant_a, name="a-widget"),
            Widget(id=uuid.uuid4(), tenant_id=tenant_b, name="b-widget"),
        ]
    )
    await db_session.commit()

    token = current_tenant_id.set(tenant_a)
    try:
        from sqlalchemy import select

        result = await db_session.execute(select(Widget))
        rows = result.scalars().all()
    finally:
        current_tenant_id.reset(token)

    assert [w.name for w in rows] == ["a-widget"]


async def test_no_current_tenant_returns_all_rows(db_session):
    install_tenancy_filter()

    db_session.add_all(
        [
            Widget(id=uuid.uuid4(), tenant_id=uuid.uuid4(), name="x"),
            Widget(id=uuid.uuid4(), tenant_id=uuid.uuid4(), name="y"),
        ]
    )
    await db_session.commit()

    from sqlalchemy import select

    result = await db_session.execute(select(Widget))
    rows = result.scalars().all()

    assert {w.name for w in rows} == {"x", "y"}


async def test_update_only_modifies_rows_for_current_tenant(db_session):
    install_tenancy_filter()

    tenant_a = uuid.uuid4()
    tenant_b = uuid.uuid4()

    widget_a_id = uuid.uuid4()
    widget_b_id = uuid.uuid4()

    db_session.add_all(
        [
            Widget(id=widget_a_id, tenant_id=tenant_a, name="a-widget"),
            Widget(id=widget_b_id, tenant_id=tenant_b, name="b-widget"),
        ]
    )
    await db_session.commit()

    # Update with tenant_a context - should only update tenant_a rows
    from sqlalchemy import update, select

    token = current_tenant_id.set(tenant_a)
    try:
        await db_session.execute(update(Widget).values(name="changed"))
        await db_session.commit()
    finally:
        current_tenant_id.reset(token)

    # Verify tenant_a row was updated
    token = current_tenant_id.set(tenant_a)
    try:
        result = await db_session.execute(select(Widget))
        tenant_a_rows = result.scalars().all()
    finally:
        current_tenant_id.reset(token)

    assert [w.name for w in tenant_a_rows] == ["changed"]

    # Verify tenant_b row was NOT updated
    token = current_tenant_id.set(tenant_b)
    try:
        result = await db_session.execute(select(Widget))
        tenant_b_rows = result.scalars().all()
    finally:
        current_tenant_id.reset(token)

    assert [w.name for w in tenant_b_rows] == ["b-widget"]


async def test_delete_only_removes_rows_for_current_tenant(db_session):
    install_tenancy_filter()

    tenant_a = uuid.uuid4()
    tenant_b = uuid.uuid4()

    widget_a_id = uuid.uuid4()
    widget_b_id = uuid.uuid4()

    db_session.add_all(
        [
            Widget(id=widget_a_id, tenant_id=tenant_a, name="a-widget"),
            Widget(id=widget_b_id, tenant_id=tenant_b, name="b-widget"),
        ]
    )
    await db_session.commit()

    # Delete with tenant_a context - should only delete tenant_a rows
    from sqlalchemy import delete, select

    token = current_tenant_id.set(tenant_a)
    try:
        await db_session.execute(delete(Widget))
        await db_session.commit()
    finally:
        current_tenant_id.reset(token)

    # Verify tenant_a row was deleted
    token = current_tenant_id.set(tenant_a)
    try:
        result = await db_session.execute(select(Widget))
        tenant_a_rows = result.scalars().all()

import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError

from app.config import Settings


def test_jwt_secret_too_short_raises_validation_error():
    """Rejects JWT secrets shorter than 32 bytes."""
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError) as exc_info:
        Settings(jwt_secret="short")
    assert "jwt_secret" in str(exc_info.value).lower()


def test_jwt_secret_default_is_long_enough():
    """Default JWT secret passes validation (32+ bytes)."""
    # Instantiate without setting JWT_SECRET env var
    # This should not raise because the default is long enough
    settings = Settings()
    assert len(settings.jwt_secret.encode("utf-8")) >= 32

import uuid

import pytest

from app.auth.models import User
from app.auth.service import (
    EmailAlreadyRegisteredError,
    InvalidRefreshTokenError,
    authenticate,
    get_user_from_refresh_token,
    register,
)
from app.core.security import create_access_token, create_refresh_token, hash_password

pytestmark = pytest.mark.asyncio


async def test_schemas_import():
    """Verify that schemas can be imported (catches missing email-validator)."""
    from app.auth.schemas import LoginRequest, RegisterRequest, TokenPair, UserOut

    assert RegisterRequest is not None
    assert LoginRequest is not None
    assert TokenPair is not None
    assert UserOut is not None


async def test_register_creates_user_with_hashed_password(db_session):
    tenant_id = uuid.uuid4()
    user = await register(
        db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email="rep@example.com", password="hunter2pass", role="rep"
    )
    assert user.email == "rep@example.com"
    assert user.role == "rep"
    assert user.hashed_password != "hunter2pass"


async def test_register_rejects_duplicate_email_in_same_tenant(db_session):
    tenant_id = uuid.uuid4()
    await register(db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email="dup@example.com", password="pass1234", role="rep")
    with pytest.raises(EmailAlreadyRegisteredError):
        await register(db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email="dup@example.com", password="pass5678", role="manager")


async def test_register_allows_same_email_in_different_tenants(db_session):
    email = "shared@example.com"
    user_a = await register(db_session, tenant_id=uuid.uuid4(), email=email, password="pass1234", role="rep")
    user_b = await register(db_session, tenant_id=uuid.uuid4(), email=email, password="pass5678", role="rep")
    assert user_a.id != user_b.id


async def test_authenticate_succeeds_with_correct_password(db_session):
    tenant_id = uuid.uuid4()
    await register(db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email="rep@example.com", password="hunter2pass", role="rep")

    user = await authenticate(db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email="rep@example.com", password="hunter2pass")
    assert user is not None
    assert user.email == "rep@example.com"


async def test_authenticate_returns_none_for_wrong_password(db_session):

    await register(db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email="rep@example.com", password="hunter2pass", role="rep")

    assert user is None

    user = await authenticate(db_session, tenant_id=uuid.uuid4(), email="ghost@example.com", password="whatever")
    assert user is None


async def test_register_race_condition_integrity_error_handling(db_session, monkeypatch):
    """Verify that IntegrityError from concurrent registrations is caught and re-raised as EmailAlreadyRegisteredError.

    This test simulates the race window: register()'s pre-check SELECT reports "no duplicate found"
    while a real duplicate row already exists and is committed. The pre-check passes but db.commit()
    then hits the uq_users_tenant_email constraint and raises IntegrityError, which must be caught
    and re-raised as EmailAlreadyRegisteredError.
    """
    tenant_id = uuid.uuid4()
    email = "race@example.com"

    # Simulate the "other" concurrent registration that already won the race and committed
    existing_user = User(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        email=email,
        hashed_password=hash_password("other-pass"),
        role="rep",
    )
    db_session.add(existing_user)
    await db_session.commit()

    # Force register()'s pre-check SELECT to report "no duplicate found" (simulating the race window
    # where this call's pre-check ran before the other one committed). Only the first execute() call
    # is faked; anything after falls through to the real session.
    class _NoMatch:
        def scalar_one_or_none(self):
            return None

    original_execute = db_session.execute
    calls = {"n": 0}

    async def fake_execute(*args, **kwargs):
        calls["n"] += 1
        if calls["n"] == 1:
            # First execute (the pre-check SELECT) returns "no match"
            return _NoMatch()
        # All subsequent execute calls use the real session
        return await original_execute(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(db_session, "execute", fake_execute)

    # register() now passes the faked pre-check, tries to INSERT, hits the real constraint, and raises IntegrityError
    with pytest.raises(EmailAlreadyRegisteredError):
        await register(db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email=email, password="hunter2pass", role="rep")

    tenant_id = uuid.uuid4()
    user = await register(
        db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email="rep@example.com", password="hunter2pass", role="rep"
    )
    refresh_token = create_refresh_token(subject=str(user.id))

    result = await get_user_from_refresh_token(db_session, refresh_token)
    assert result.id == user.id

    tenant_id = uuid.uuid4()
    user = await register(
        db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email="rep@example.com", password="hunter2pass", role="rep"
    )
    access_token = create_access_token(subject=str(user.id), role="rep", tenant_id=str(tenant_id))

    with pytest.raises(InvalidRefreshTokenError):
        await get_user_from_refresh_token(db_session, access_token)

    with pytest.raises(InvalidRefreshTokenError):
        await get_user_from_refresh_token(db_session, "not-a-real-jwt")


async def test_get_user_from_refresh_token_rejects_unknown_user(db_session):
    """Token is well-formed and unexpired, but the user it points to doesn't exist
    (e.g. deleted after the refresh token was issued)."""
    refresh_token = create_refresh_token(subject=str(uuid.uuid4()))

    with pytest.raises(InvalidRefreshTokenError):
        await get_user_from_refresh_token(db_session, refresh_token)

Your tests should expect `ValidationError`, not bare `ValueError` — pydantic wraps validator errors, which is exactly why the existing length test uses `pytest.raises(ValidationError)`; mirror it. Also confirm no `.env`/`JWT_SECRET` is set in the test env, or `Settings(environment="production")` won't use the default and won't raise.

import uuid

import jwt
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.auth.models import User
from app.core.security import decode_token, hash_password, verify_password


class EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(Exception):
    pass


class InvalidRefreshTokenError(Exception):
    pass


async def register(
    db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str, password: str, role: str
) -> User:
    existing = await db.execute(
        select(User).where(User.tenant_id == tenant_id, User.email == email)
    )
    if existing.scalar_one_or_none() is not None:
        raise EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(email)

    user = User(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        email=email,
        hashed_password=hash_password(password),
        role=role,
    )
    db.add(user)
    try:
        await db.commit()
    except IntegrityError:
        await db.rollback()
        raise EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(email)
    await db.refresh(user)
    return user


async def authenticate(
    db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str, password: str
) -> User | None:
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.tenant_id == tenant_id, User.email == email))
    user = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if user is None:
        return None
    if not verify_password(password, user.hashed_password):
        return None
    return user


async def get_user_by_id(db: AsyncSession, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> User | None:
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()


async def get_user_from_refresh_token(db: AsyncSession, refresh_token: str) -> User:
    """Validates a refresh token and returns the user it belongs to.

    Raises InvalidRefreshTokenError if the token is malformed, expired, not a
    refresh token (e.g. an access token was passed instead), or the user no
    longer exists.
    """
    try:
        payload = decode_token(refresh_token)
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError() from exc

    if payload.get("type") != "refresh":
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError()

    user = await get_user_by_id(db, uuid.UUID(payload["sub"]))
    if user is None:
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError()

    return user

import uuid

import jwt
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.auth.models import User
from app.core.security import decode_token, hash_password, verify_password


class EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(Exception):
    pass


class InvalidRefreshTokenError(Exception):
    pass


async def _get_by_tenant_email(db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str) -> User | None:
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.tenant_id == tenant_id, User.email == email))
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()


async def register(
    db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str, password: str, role: str
) -> User:
    existing = await _get_by_tenant_email(db, tenant_id, email)
    if existing is not None:
        raise EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(email)

    user = User(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        email=email,
        hashed_password=hash_password(password),
        role=role,
    )
    db.add(user)
    try:
        await db.commit()
    except IntegrityError:
        await db.rollback()
        raise EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(email)
    await db.refresh(user)
    return user


async def authenticate(
    db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str, password: str
) -> User | None:
    user = await _get_by_tenant_email(db, tenant_id, email)
    if user is None:
        return None
    if not verify_password(password, user.hashed_password):
        return None
    return user


async def get_user_by_id(db: AsyncSession, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> User | None:
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()


async def get_user_from_refresh_token(db: AsyncSession, refresh_token: str) -> User:
    """Validates a refresh token and returns the user it belongs to.

    Raises InvalidRefreshTokenError if the token is malformed, expired, not a
    refresh token (e.g. an access token was passed instead), or the user no
    longer exists.
    """
    try:
        payload = decode_token(refresh_token)
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError() from exc

    if payload.get("type") != "refresh":
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError()

    user = await get_user_by_id(db, uuid.UUID(payload["sub"]))
    if user is None:
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError()

    return user

async def test_register_race_condition_integrity_error_handling(db_session, monkeypatch):
    """Verify that IntegrityError from concurrent registrations is caught and re-raised as EmailAlreadyRegisteredError.

    This test simulates the race window: register()'s pre-check SELECT reports "no duplicate found"
    while a real duplicate row already exists and is committed. The pre-check passes but db.commit()
    then hits the uq_users_tenant_email constraint and raises IntegrityError, which must be caught
    and re-raised as EmailAlreadyRegisteredError.
    """
    tenant_id = uuid.uuid4()
    email = "race@example.com"

    # Simulate the "other" concurrent registration that already won the race and committed
    existing_user = User(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        email=email,
        hashed_password=hash_password("other-pass"),
        role="rep",
    )
    db_session.add(existing_user)
    await db_session.commit()

    # Force register()'s pre-check SELECT to report "no duplicate found" (simulating the race window
    # where this call's pre-check ran before the other one committed). Only the first execute() call
    # is faked; anything after falls through to the real session.
    class _NoMatch:
        def scalar_one_or_none(self):
            return None

    original_execute = db_session.execute
    calls = {"n": 0}

    async def fake_execute(*args, **kwargs):
        calls["n"] += 1
        if calls["n"] == 1:
            # First execute (the pre-check SELECT) returns "no match"
            return _NoMatch()
        # All subsequent execute calls use the real session
        return await original_execute(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(db_session, "execute", fake_execute)

    # register() now passes the faked pre-check, tries to INSERT, hits the real constraint, and raises IntegrityError
    with pytest.raises(EmailAlreadyRegisteredError):
        await register(db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email=email, password="hunter2pass", role="rep")

    )
    refresh_token = create_refresh_token(subject=str(user.id))

    assert result.id == user.id

import uuid
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

import jwt
from fastapi import Depends, Header, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.auth.models import User
from app.auth.service import get_user_by_id
from app.core.security import decode_token
from app.core.tenancy import current_tenant_id
from app.db import get_db

oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="/api/v1/auth/login", auto_error=False)


async def get_tenant_id(x_tenant_id: str = Header(...)) -> uuid.UUID:
    try:
        return uuid.UUID(x_tenant_id)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST, detail="invalid tenant id") from exc


async def get_current_user(
    token: str | None = Depends(oauth2_scheme),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> AsyncIterator[User]:
    credentials_error = HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
        detail="could not validate credentials",
        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
    )
    if token is None:
        raise credentials_error

    try:
        payload = decode_token(token)
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
        raise credentials_error from exc

    if payload.get("type") != "access":
        raise credentials_error

    user = await get_user_by_id(db, uuid.UUID(payload["sub"]))
    if user is None:
        raise credentials_error

    # Scope current_tenant_id to this request only. FastAPI runs a yield
    # dependency's post-yield code as teardown after the route handler
    # returns, so the reset always fires - unlike a plain `return`, which
    # would leave the ContextVar set for whatever runs next in this context.
    reset_token = current_tenant_id.set(user.tenant_id)
    try:
        yield user

import uuid

import jwt
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.auth.models import User
from app.core.security import decode_token, hash_password, verify_password


class EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(Exception):
    pass


class InvalidRefreshTokenError(Exception):
    pass


# Precomputed once at import time so authenticate() can pay the same argon2
# verification cost for an unknown email as it does for a known one with a
# wrong password - otherwise "unknown email" responds fast (no hashing) while
# "known email, wrong password" is slow, letting an attacker enumerate
# registered emails by timing.
_DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH = hash_password("dummy-password-for-timing-parity")


async def _get_by_tenant_email(db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str) -> User | None:
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.tenant_id == tenant_id, User.email == email))
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()


async def register(
    db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str, password: str, role: str
) -> User:
    existing = await _get_by_tenant_email(db, tenant_id, email)
    if existing is not None:
        raise EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(email)

    user = User(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        email=email,
        hashed_password=hash_password(password),
        role=role,
    )
    db.add(user)
    try:
        await db.commit()
    except IntegrityError:
        await db.rollback()
        raise EmailAlreadyRegisteredError(email)
    await db.refresh(user)
    return user


async def authenticate(
    db: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, email: str, password: str
) -> User | None:
    user = await _get_by_tenant_email(db, tenant_id, email)
    if user is None:
        verify_password(password, _DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH)
        return None
    if not verify_password(password, user.hashed_password):
        return None
    return user


async def get_user_by_id(db: AsyncSession, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> User | None:
    result = await db.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()


async def get_user_from_refresh_token(db: AsyncSession, refresh_token: str) -> User:
    """Validates a refresh token and returns the user it belongs to.

    Raises InvalidRefreshTokenError if the token is malformed, expired, not a
    refresh token (e.g. an access token was passed instead), or the user no
    longer exists.
    """
    try:
        payload = decode_token(refresh_token)
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError() from exc

    if payload.get("type") != "refresh":
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError()

    user = await get_user_by_id(db, uuid.UUID(payload["sub"]))
    if user is None:
        raise InvalidRefreshTokenError()

    return user

    """Regression test for timing-based user enumeration: an unknown email must

async def test_register_race_condition_integrity_error_handling(db_session, monkeypatch):
    """Verify that IntegrityError from concurrent registrations is caught and re-raised as EmailAlreadyRegisteredError.

    This test simulates the race window: register()'s pre-check SELECT reports "no duplicate found"
    while a real duplicate row already exists and is committed. The pre-check passes but db.commit()
    then hits the uq_users_tenant_email constraint and raises IntegrityError, which must be caught
    and re-raised as EmailAlreadyRegisteredError.
    """
    tenant_id = uuid.uuid4()
    email = "race@example.com"

    # Simulate the "other" concurrent registration that already won the race and committed
    existing_user = User(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        email=email,
        hashed_password=hash_password("other-pass"),
        role="rep",
    )
    db_session.add(existing_user)
    await db_session.commit()

    # Force register()'s pre-check SELECT to report "no duplicate found" (simulating the race window
    # where this call's pre-check ran before the other one committed). Only the first execute() call
    # is faked; anything after falls through to the real session.
    class _NoMatch:
        def scalar_one_or_none(self):
            return None

    original_execute = db_session.execute
    calls = {"n": 0}

    async def fake_execute(*args, **kwargs):
        calls["n"] += 1
        if calls["n"] == 1:
            # First execute (the pre-check SELECT) returns "no match"
            return _NoMatch()
        # All subsequent execute calls use the real session
        return await original_execute(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(db_session, "execute", fake_execute)

    # register() now passes the faked pre-check, tries to INSERT, hits the real constraint, and raises IntegrityError
    with pytest.raises(EmailAlreadyRegisteredError):
        await register(db_session, tenant_id=tenant_id, email=email, password="hunter2pass", role="rep")

# PLAN.md — Atlas Field Force Build Order

See [`docs/design.md`](docs/design.md) for the approved design. Detailed step-by-step implementation plan lives wherever `superpowers:writing-plans` writes it (linked from PROGRESS.md once created).

## Phase 0 — Repo scaffold & state files
- [x] 0.1 Repo created (private), README, design spec, research doc, this file, PROGRESS.md

## Phase 1 — Backend core
- [ ] 1.1 FastAPI app skeleton, config, async DB session, `uv` project, Alembic init
- [ ] 1.2 Multi-tenancy base: `tenant_id` on a base model mixin, session-level filter
- [ ] 1.3 Auth: `reps`/`managers` (or a unified `users` table with a role column), JWT access+refresh, argon2
- [ ] 1.4 In-process event bus + in-process background job runner (mirrors Atlas's `core/events`, `core/jobs`)

## Phase 2 — Zones & geofencing
- [ ] 2.1 `zones` (GeoJSON polygon), `zone_assignments`
- [ ] 2.2 Point-in-polygon service (pure Python), unit tests incl. edge cases (on boundary, antimeridian not required)

## Phase 3 — Location pings
- [ ] 3.1 Ping ingestion endpoint (idempotency-keyed), `location_pings` table + indexes
- [ ] 3.2 Retention/downsample background job

## Phase 4 — Visits & tasks
- [ ] 4.1 `visits`: check-in/out, geofence-verified flag, notes, photo upload, `external_reference`
- [ ] 4.2 `tasks`: CRUD, assignment, due dates, priority, completion

## Phase 5 — Goals
- [ ] 5.1 `goals`: VISIT_COUNT / TASK_COUNT / SALES_VALUE (manual entry), target-vs-achievement report endpoint

## Phase 6 — Violations & alerts
- [ ] 6.1 Zone-violation detection (on ping ingestion, rep outside assigned zone during work hours)
- [ ] 6.2 `ZoneViolationDetected` event → web push (VAPID) to subscribed managers + dashboard flag

## Phase 7 — Manager web dashboard
- [ ] 7.1 Scaffold (Vite+React+TS+Tailwind), auth, API client
- [ ] 7.2 Live map (Leaflet), polling
- [ ] 7.3 Zone drawing (leaflet-draw)
- [ ] 7.4 Task/goal admin, violations feed, push-subscription opt-in

## Phase 8 — Tablet app (Android)
- [ ] 8.1 Capacitor+React scaffold, login
- [ ] 8.2 Background location plugin (open-source path) + ping posting
- [ ] 8.3 Offline queue (pings, check-ins, task updates, photos) + sync-on-reconnect
- [ ] 8.4 Check-in/out, task list, goal progress view

## Phase 9 — Tests & CI
- [ ] 9.1 Backend unit/integration tests mirror source; `tests/perf/` for ping ingestion
- [ ] 9.2 CI workflow: backend lint+test, dashboard typecheck+build, tablet app build

## Phase 10 — Deployability (not deployment)
- [ ] 10.1 Dockerfile(s) + docker-compose, migrations verified end-to-end locally
- [ ] 10.2 README quickstart
- [ ] 10.3 Punch list of what's left that requires customer/user input (domain, VAPID keys, cloud provider, real-device GPS testing)

## Scope-cut rule

If time pressure forces a cut: cut dashboard polish before backend correctness, and tablet polish before offline-sync correctness (a lost visit is worse than an ugly screen).

A passing result in the full suite alone would prove little, because `_installed` is a process-global that never resets — any earlier test that installs the filter would mask a missing `create_app()` call. What makes your test load-bearing is the **isolation proof**: fresh process, filter fails-open (both rows leak) before the fix, filters correctly after. That's the evidence; the full-suite pass is corroboration, not proof. Also state the residual: the in-suite guarantee currently depends on file collection order (`auth/` before `core/`), so a future `pytest-randomly` or a rename could let it pass without the fix — the isolation run is what you'd re-run to re-verify. SQLite collapses `DateTime()` and `DateTime(timezone=True)` to the same type, so that check only proves the migration *applies*; agreement here is by inspection (both sides now explicitly `timezone=True`). An autogenerate-diff check wouldn't add anything on SQLite — inspection is the right verification, just describe it as such.

# Final whole-branch review — fix report

Branch: `feat/backend-core-phase1`

| 2 | `97d1b1f` | fix(backend): make created_at timezone-aware in model and migration |
| 3 | `7e5f0dd` | fix(backend): reject default JWT secret outside development |

| 4 | `0a8863c` | fix(backend): pay hashing cost for unknown email in authenticate() |
| 6 | `66573bc` | fix(backend): handle malformed sub claim without 500ing |
| 7 | `3a99aff` | docs: mark Phase 1 complete, log final-review findings in PROGRESS.md |

Note on ordering: Fix 5 (extract `_get_by_tenant_email` helper) was done immediately
before Fix 4 (timing-safe `authenticate()`), rather than after it as numbered in the
task, so that `authenticate()`'s body is only edited once instead of once per fix.
Pure reordering — every fix's content matches its numbered spec below.

Test count: 43 (baseline before any fix) → **50** (after all fixes), +7 new tests.
Final `uv run pytest -v`: **50 passed**. Final `uv run ruff check .`: **All checks passed!**

---

## Fix 1 (Critical): tenant-isolation filter never installed in the running app

**Problem confirmed by reading the code before touching it:** `backend/app/main.py`'s
`create_app()` built the `FastAPI()` instance and mounted the auth router but never
called `app.core.tenancy.install_tenancy_filter()`. That function registers a
SQLAlchemy `do_orm_execute` listener on the `Session` class that scopes every
`TenantScopedMixin`-backed query to `current_tenant_id`. Only test files
(`tests/core/test_tenancy.py`) called it directly. In a real running process, the
listener was simply never registered — every query, from every request, ran
completely unscoped by tenant, regardless of what `current_tenant_id` held.

Verified the filter's early-return behavior is still intact before relying on it:
`_apply_tenant_filter` in `tenancy.py` returns immediately when
`current_tenant_id.get() is None`, so wiring the filter in changes nothing for
register/login/refresh, which all run with the ContextVar unset.

**Fix:** Added `install_tenancy_filter()` call in `create_app()`
(`backend/app/main.py`), right after `FastAPI()` construction:

```python
def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(title="Atlas Field Force", version="0.1.0")
    install_tenancy_filter()
    ...
```

**Regression test (`backend/tests/auth/test_router.py::test_tenancy_filter_is_live_via_create_app`):**
Registers a user in tenant A and a different user in tenant B through the real
`client`/`app` fixture (built via `create_app()`, no manual `install_tenancy_filter()`
call anywhere in the test), then — sharing the same underlying test-db engine via the
`db_session` fixture — runs a raw `select(User)` with `current_tenant_id` set to
tenant A and asserts only tenant A's row comes back.

**Test evidence — TDD, both directions:**
1. Wrote the test against the *unfixed* `main.py` and ran it in isolation
   (`uv run pytest tests/auth/test_router.py::test_tenancy_filter_is_live_via_create_app -v`,

## Concerns

**Fix 1 is the load-bearing fix, and here is the honest account of the test's
strength and its limits, as requested:**

The regression test is **not weak**, but its strength comes specifically from how it
was verified, not from the fact that it currently passes. `tenancy._installed` is a
plain module-level boolean that is set once and never reset for the lifetime of the
Python process. That means a bare "does the test pass in the full suite" check would
prove very little on its own — if any earlier-collected test file had already called
`install_tenancy_filter()` directly (as `tests/core/test_tenancy.py` does), the flag
would already be `True` by the time a later test ran, and a functional filter-check
test would pass *regardless of whether `create_app()` calls the installer* — silently
masking the exact bug this fix addresses. That is precisely the failure mode the task
warned about for the existing unit-level test, and it would apply equally to a naive
new one.

What actually makes this test load-bearing is that it was run **in isolation, in a
fresh process, against the unfixed code**, and it failed with tenant B's data leaking
into a tenant-A-scoped query — then passed once the one-line fix was applied. That's
empirical proof the fix is necessary and sufficient, not an assumption from a
passing full-suite run.

**Residual risk to flag:** within the *current* full-suite run, the test's correctness
also happens to be corroborated by file collection order — `tests/auth/` sorts before
`tests/core/`, so this test's `client`/`app` fixture is the first thing in the whole
suite to trigger filter installation, meaning `create_app()` (not some other test) is
demonstrably what flips the flag when the suite runs top to bottom. But this is
incidental, not load-bearing: if test collection order changes (alphabetical directory
listing changes, `pytest-randomly` gets added, files get renamed/moved), the in-suite
ordering guarantee could disappear, though the test's *pass/fail correctness* would
not — it would still correctly detect a missing `install_tenancy_filter()` call
whenever it happens to run first, and would still be provable by the same isolated-run
method used here. If this ever needs re-verifying (e.g. before a future refactor of
`create_app()` or `tenancy.py`), re-run the isolated command:

```
uv run pytest tests/auth/test_router.py::test_tenancy_filter_is_live_via_create_app -v
```

as a fresh process — that is the check that actually exercises the guarantee, not a
full-suite pass.

No other concerns. All fixes were scoped exactly to what the task specified — no
speculative extra abstractions were added (e.g. no new exception hierarchy for Fix 6
beyond reusing the existing `credentials_error`/`InvalidRefreshTokenError` paths, no
config object or settings class for the Fix 3 default-secret constant beyond a single
module-level string).
